title: Taking the Liability of a Line Outside Cover From the Claim Record
content:
The liability of the lines restated on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is measured from the record, and which figure on the record is taken depends on what those lines show.

> *The record shows.* The lines record the policyholder owing an amount.
> *The figure taken.* That recorded amount is taken as the liability restated.

> *The record shows.* The lines record nothing owing, but the supplement paid on them.
> *The figure taken.* What the supplement paid on them is taken as the liability restated.

> *The record shows.* Neither of those.
> *The figure taken.* Nothing is taken as the liability of those lines.

### Points of judgement

The first case is reached wherever the lines outside cover record the policyholder owing an amount, and the figure is that recorded amount as it stands, not what the supplement paid.

The second case is reached only where the lines record nothing owing at all. The figure is then what the supplement paid on those lines.

Where the lines record nothing owing and the supplement paid nothing on them, nothing is taken as their liability.

### Hypothetical figures

Two lines outside cover, each recording the policyholder owing 45.00: the recorded amount of 90.00 is taken as the liability restated.

Two lines outside cover recording nothing owing, on which the supplement paid 138.00: that 138.00 is taken as the liability restated.
